findings.disposition: 2026-10-11: one id (the request id, traceId) now reaches the turn input, a Temporal memo (spaceTraceId, traceparent, w3cTraceId), worker activity records with reasonCode and category, and TURN_FAILED events; GET /api/admin/traces/:traceId returns the causal error with ids, codes and statuses only. Injected faults map to categories (TOOL_UNAVAILABLE, TIMEOUT, PROTOCOL, STATE_MISSING, TEMPORAL_UNAVAILABLE). Local metrics without external telemetry: API /metrics (CPU, event-loop delay, errors by code/category, Temporal backlog and age, workflow starts, retries, CLI disconnect/reconnect), restricted to loopback/private clients and admins; opt-in loopback worker and Temporal SDK metrics; W3C traceparent continued without OpenTelemetry. Open: supervisor child failures carry generic text (needs patched()), mission/task rows lack trace columns, background continuations start new traces, memory workers and CLI/browser hosts have no metrics; span export exists since 2026-10-12 as optional OTLP/HTTP JSON for API request spans (SPACE_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, off by default, fd377fdb83), still without worker/host spans. 2026-10-12 (c68d980079): the CLI and Browser Hosts are covered by metrics the API observes (space_host_up, start time, resident memory and CPU from /proc after a command-line check, CLI sessions by status and attachments, browser sessions and live workloads against their limits), so the hosts need no endpoint of their own and no restart. Still open: memory-worker metrics, worker/host spans, trace columns on mission/task rows. 2026-10-12 (8ad3e77858): the memory-maintenance and memory-mutation workers are in /metrics too (space_host_up, start time, resident memory, CPU), found in /proc by command line at most every 15 s, with no worker change or restart. 2026-10-27 (goal e803a663, plan clipboard:zJF0KEWRcCje step 4): done since this entry was written: worker and both memory workers export OTLP activity spans under the caller's traceparent (2026-10-16), Room Agent missions and task runs carry trace_id and error_code (migration 0206), and supervisor failures keep their cause as an error code (31e2d2ef23, EXT-G-5). New: a CLI session keeps the request that allocated it (pane_cli_sessions.trace_id, migration 0258) and /api/admin/traces/:traceId returns cliSessions with their cliTaskId and cliTaskRevisionId (cli-terminal-control.test.ts end to end through the route; room-agent-trace-postgres.test.ts on a disposable PostgreSQL). Still open: CLI and Browser Host spans (host code ships only with the guarded host restart), collector scrape of the worker's loopback metrics endpoints, recovery counters beyond plan retries, terminal reconnects and activity retries. 2026-10-28 (goal e803a663, plan clipboard:zJF0KEWRcCje step 9): the three recovery counters this line names already existed: plan retries as space_recovery_events_total{kind="plan_model_retry"} (apps/api/src/api-metrics.ts), terminal reconnects as space_cli_terminal_reconnects_total{source,outcome} with the server's REATTACHED and the client's SCHEDULED/SUCCEEDED/STOPPED/SESSION_RECOVERED (observability-metrics.test.ts), activity retries as space_worker_activity_retries_total (apps/worker/src/worker-metrics.ts). New: kind browser_stream_host counts a Browser Host restart that ends live browser viewers (SCHEDULED, the pages reconnect) and a host that stays unreadable (FAILED), once per host-watch end, not per viewer (browser-stream-host-watch.ts; test: the OBS-001 case in browser-stream-host-watch.test.ts). Still open: CLI and Browser Host spans, collector scrape of the worker's loopback metrics endpoints. 2026-10-28 later (plan clipboard:zJF0KEWRcCje step 4): the collector cannot reach public-host's loopback, so the API now relays each worker endpoint on stable at GET /api/metrics/scrape/<target> (worker 9469, worker-temporal 9464, memory-maintenance 9470, memory-mutation 9471, the units' ports) under /api/metrics/scrape's rule (the collector's bearer token from a private-network address); unknown target 404, silent endpoint 503, no targets on dev (its loopback would answer with stable's workers). apps/api/src/metrics-scrape.ts; tests: the relay and unit-port cases in apps/api/tests/metrics-scrape.test.ts; docs/quality/observability.md. Still open: the four scrape jobs on the collector (CT 210, outside this repository; they work once the change is on stable after the operator's promote), and CLI and Browser Host spans (guarded host restart). 2026-10-28 13:45 UTC (Nous decision A): the collector scrapes them: after promote q-20261028-133714-a382 put the relay on stable (a9ad4d493f), CT 210's prometheus.yml got four jobs shaped like space_api (space_worker, space_worker_temporal, space_memory_maintenance, space_memory_mutation; same token file, label space_service), with a dated backup beside it, promtool check config and a SIGHUP reload; 80 s later all 77 targets were up (the 73 before unchanged) and each new job stored samples. Still open: CLI and Browser Host spans (guarded host restart). 2026-11-02 (goal e803a663, plan clipboard:zJF0KEWRcCje step 4; commit 5caa150021, ticket q-20261102-003020-15cd DEPLOYED on dev 2d48e784a4, live:verify:dev ok): the API already passed its request or trace id (req:<id>, Nous trace:<24 hex>) into every sendInput and Browser Host call; it now reaches the hosts. The pane hosts take it on attach and input (CliHostAttachInput.traceId, CliHostClient.input traceId) and write one cli_host_request line per traced request; the Browser Host manager (traceBrowserHostCalls in apps/api/src/browser-sessions.ts) writes one browser_host_request line for navigate, action, pages, control, viewport, stream, stop, capture and Vault fill (per-keystroke input and lease heartbeats left out). Each line holds method, trace id, session or pane, status, error code and duration, never input text or a URL. GET /api/admin/traces/:traceId names both greps (logQueries.cliHost, logQueries.browserHost). Tests: the OBS-001 cases in packages/cli-host/tests/ipc.test.ts and apps/api/tests/browser-host-trace.test.ts (both fail without the change), the logQueries lines in trace-correlation.test.ts, the trace id lines in cli-runtimes.test.ts and cli-runtimes-host.test.ts. Still open: the lines start only with the guarded pane-host and Browser Host restarts after the promote, so the live end-to-end proof (one pane CLI request and one browser request found under one id) waits for them; the hosts write log lines, not OTLP spans. 2026-11-02 evening, live on stable (goal e803a663, plan clipboard:zJF0KEWRcCje step 4; read only, no code change): the host trace code (5caa150021) reached stable with promote 05d3be9cc7 (02:35 EET) and both hosts restarted after it (Browser Host 10:08 EET, pane host 11:12 EET), so no restart is left to wait for. From those restarts to 18:06 EET the pane host wrote 1,422 cli_host_request lines (attach 690, input 719, terminate 13; 987 trace ids: API requests, Nous turns, copilot kickoffs, schedules) and the Browser Host 2,161 browser_host_request lines (2,146 ids; action 1,925, stopPane 105, activatePage 30, vaultFill 29, createPage 25, closePage 24, control 21, navigate 1, setStreamMode 1). The fields are only event, method, trace id, pane, CLI session or error code, status and duration, never input text or a URL. Each id leads back to the API: req:ROL0s9eJUBu7 is both the API's SOCKET_ATTACHED lifecycle event and the pane host's attach line for the same CLI session and pane; 515 Browser Host lines carry an id the API's own log names as its request (e.g. createPage under POST /api/cli/browser/commands, stopPane under POST /api/cli/browser/commands). No request in that window touched both hosts, so no single id is in both journals; the trace lookup greps each journal by the id, so it needs none. Still open: the hosts write JSON log lines, not OTLP spans (host code, shipped only with the guarded host restarts). 2026-11-02, closed as accepted-tradeoff (Nous's decision A on the evening's needs-decision): the hosts' JSON trace lines (cli_host_request, browser_host_request) are their trace; each request id greps back to the API's own line for that request. OTLP host spans would add no new lookup and cost two guarded host restarts (pane host and Browser Host). If a real need appears, OTLP spans in packages/cli-host and the Browser Host can ride a future guarded restart of those hosts.

findings.observation: 'Pinned, verified images' while compose pulled mutable tags without a digest check
findings.observationSource: Independent review of the v1.1.4 snapshot (public 837e0b0), 2026-10-14
findings.evidence: packages/run-spaceapp/templates/images.lock.json and compose.yml, src/image-attestations.mjs (public); published run-spaceapp 1.1.9 (npm latest): its own verifyLockedImages run against ghcr.io on 2026-10-31 passed for core, cli and browser on amd64 and arm64 (SBOM and SLSA provenance from oll4com/spaceapp release.yml on main, commit 4e648e7, run 40813047247); the 1.1.9 tags resolve to the locked index digests; npm provenance (SLSA v1, release.yml, refs/heads/main) matches the tarball's sha512
findings.disposition: Public 813b76b: pgvector, Temporal and codex-lb are pinned by multi-arch index digest (headroom already was); the README and security model now say that SpaceApp images are pulled by exact version tag, which the release workflow publishes once (it fails closed when a tag exists) with SBOM and provenance attestations it verifies. Open: verifying the first-party digest or attestation at install time. Internal review 1.1.5 Codex #9: still open for SpaceApp's own images; planned for 1.1.7. External review 2026-10-16 #8. 2026-10-17: public overlay 219b4c0 (ships in run-spaceapp 1.1.7, with the codex-sessions-init service pinned too): after the images are published and verified, the release writes their digests into the tested npm package (templates/images.lock.json, the only allowed difference) and the launcher pulls name:version@sha256; the devtest probe accepts pinned images. Proven only by the next real publish. 1.1.8 (public overlay branch, task:6sCDD1rdjPyC): before an installation first uses a locked version, the launcher checks its images (packages/run-spaceapp/src/image-attestations.mjs): every platform image in each pinned index needs an SBOM and an SLSA provenance statement about that exact image from oll4com/spaceapp's release.yml on main, all read by digest from the pinned index; it records the run and commit in image-attestations.json and stops before pulling otherwise. The release's verify-published-containers.mjs runs the same check, with this run's commit for a full release. The reads use HTTPS_PROXY / NO_PROXY, or else the Docker client's proxies.default in ~/.docker/config.json; an unreachable registry stops with those settings named, and a failed check stops whatever the proxy settings. Known limitation: SPACEAPP_IMAGE_VERIFY=off skips the check on air-gapped or locked-down hosts; every launcher run then warns, and the version stays recorded as unverified until a run without it verifies it. Checked read-only against the published 1.1.7 images (run 39996418646, f1c4e83), directly and through a CONNECT proxy. 1.1.8 was never published; its changes ship in 1.1.9. 2026-10-31 (plan clipboard:NtzEOzE3Ew00 step 4): run-spaceapp 1.1.9 is published and npm latest; its package carries templates/images.lock.json (core, cli and browser index digests) and the launcher writes them into compose as name:1.1.9@sha256. The published package's own pre-pull check (verifyLockedImages, the code an install runs before it first uses a version) was run read only against ghcr.io: all six platform images passed, each with an SBOM and an SLSA provenance statement from release.yml on main at 4e648e7 (run 40813047247); the 1.1.9 tags resolve to the same index digests; the npm tarball's SLSA provenance names release.yml on refs/heads/main and matches its sha512. Pulling by digest makes Docker check the content, so no separate RepoDigests read is needed. SPACEAPP_IMAGE_VERIFY=off stays the documented opt-out for air-gapped hosts (it warns on every run). A full install from the registry on a test VM is part of P8's post-publish run. 2026-11-02 (goal e803a663, plan clipboard:NtzEOzE3Ew00 step 4): every image SpaceApp builds or ships on the 1.2.0 line (public feat/public-nous-1.2 4f255e9) was checked; none is left unpinned or without provenance, so no code changed. Dockerfile bases are node:<version>-trixie-slim@sha256 (public-docker-distribution.test.mjs requires the exact pin; the Node 26 branch keeps one); compose pins pgvector, Temporal, codex-lb and headroom-codex-lb by index digest (compose-images.test.mjs) and SpaceApp core, cli and browser through images.lock.json; every GitHub Action is pinned by commit SHA; the published builds carry SBOM and SLSA provenance (mode=max), while the CI candidate builds keep provenance: false because they are loaded locally (push: false, load: true) and a loaded image cannot hold an attestation manifest. headroom-codex-lb, the one shipped image built outside release.yml, carries buildkit SLSA provenance for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 naming github.com/oll4com/headroom-codex-lb at 5b153195 (its tag code-5b15319), read only from ghcr.io. The Space-side deploy/docx-normalizer base is debian:trixie-slim@sha256. image-lock and image-attestations tests 12/12 on the 1.2 line. 2026-11-02 later (Nous decision, plan clipboard:NtzEOzE3Ew00 step 4): code done. The install-of-a-published-package evidence comes from run-spaceapp 1.2.0's next-to-latest lab run (plan clipboard:NtXOwLkXVN1x step 8, before any dist-tag latest): the exact commands and the output folder are in ~/agent-workspace/active/20261030-public-nous-1.2/LAB-PLAN.md, section "After publish: shipped-image evidence before latest" (records under ~/agent-workspace/reports/<date>-run-spaceapp-1.2.0-shipped-images/, verdict shipped-image-evidence.json); no 1.1.9 lab install will be made. 2026-11-02 later (plan clipboard:NtzEOzE3Ew00 step 4): the earlier check covered the public line; Space's own root docker-compose.yml (this host's Postgres and Temporal) still named pgvector, Temporal server, admin-tools and UI by tag. Each is now pinned by index digest. pgvector is pinned at 7a7e9f22, the build this host runs (container image 36b64a4e), not the tag's newer 01215e09, so a later compose up recreates the containers on the same image. scripts/tests/compose-image-digests.test.mjs (in test:deploy) fails on a tag-only image. Provenance: Space's own local build (deploy/docx-normalizer, base pinned) is loaded locally and never pushed, so it can hold no attestation; the four third-party images carry whatever their publishers attach.

findings.observationSource: Independent review of the v1.1.4 snapshot (public 837e0b0), 2026-10-14
findings.evidence: apps/api/tests/child-process-env.test.ts; apps/worker/tests/child-process-env.test.ts; packages/gateway/tests/local-embeddings.test.ts; scripts/tests/child-process-env-guard.test.mjs (npm run test:deploy, run by the merge queue); apps/worker/tests/support/child-process-env-scan.mjs; ~/agent-workspace/active/20261102-ext-c-f8-children/inventory.md
findings.disposition: e851e2f128: childProcessEnv() removes Space credentials from every spawn in apps/api; a test keeps process.env spreads out. Internal review 1.1.5 found the claim overstated; see INT5-C-F5. 2026-10-30, 6b0a6cebe9 (goal e803a663): the single childProcessEnv policy now lives in @space/runtime; the API keeps a compatibility re-export. Credential-free SQLite children in the worker and runtime, API video/tool-status and Design/Media Chrome/ffmpeg/broker children, Nous provider/auth-reader utility children, and the API-used queue Git helper now set filtered environments explicitly. Existing worker broker, OpenCode probe and Codex App Server allowlists remain intact. One worker guard checks raw process.env spreads and omitted env options in the audited paths; removing the SQLite env makes it fail. Scoped API/worker/runtime/script/queue tests passed (101 tests, including real child-process and Chrome render/lifecycle tests). One documented privileged exception, approved by the operator at 03:45 BKK: run-with-space-env.mjs -> cli-maintenance-runner.mjs remains unchanged because SPACE_DATABASE_URL is required to read/update durable maintenance records; a credential-scoped loader is not part of this step. Resolution stays partial: protected packages/cli-host/src/server.ts and packages/browser-host/src/server.ts still have inheriting Git identity children, node-pty-spawn.ts forwards caller-supplied spec.env and needs its separate host audit, and the public container core-entrypoint/core-supervisor web-proxy inheritance remains unverified. No host, Warm or public-installer code changed. This is not a blanket claim for standalone scripts or services: the gateway local Python child and separate queue deployment daemon are outside the API/worker utility scope. 2026-10-30 later (plan clipboard:zJF0KEWRcCje): of the services that load /opt/spaceapp/.env, the API, worker and memory workers were covered; space-gateway (EnvironmentFile=/opt/spaceapp/.env, active) still started its local embedding worker (packages/gateway/src/providers/local/embeddings.ts, Python on bge-m3) with no env, so it inherited SPACE_SESSION_SECRET and SPACE_DATABASE_URL. It now gets childProcessEnv() from @space/runtime (the gateway bundle already loads @space/runtime through @space/db; the dependency is now declared), and the worker guard lists the file: on the previous line it fails with embeddings.ts:70 missing or raw env. The real bge-m3 test on this host's CPU passes with the filtered environment. Checked and left: space-codex-update.timer (update-codex-cli.sh) runs with .env but every deploy disables it; space-cli-maintenance-check's scheduler spawns nothing; space-web spawns nothing; OpenCode shared and the DeepSeek Harness load their own env files. Step 30 of the same plan adds a behavioural guard in the gateway itself: packages/gateway/tests/local-embeddings.test.ts starts the worker through a stand-in python with a fake SPACE_SESSION_SECRET and SPACE_DATABASE_URL in the gateway environment and fails when either reaches the child (proved by dropping env from the spawn). Still partial for the reasons above (pane host, Browser Host, node-pty-spawn.ts, public container entrypoint/supervisor; the queue daemon; the approved maintenance-runner exception). 2026-11-02 (plan clipboard:zJF0KEWRcCje, 9a05944db3): a whole-tree audit (every spawn/exec/execFile/fork and node-pty call in apps, packages, scripts and deploy) checked against the installed systemd units, not only deploy/, found one more inheriting child: space-db-cleanup.service (User=space, EnvironmentFile=/opt/spaceapp/.env, timer enabled) ran scripts/space-db-cleanup.mjs, whose docker inspect fallback had no env; it now gets childProcessEnv(). The worker guard no longer uses a fixed package list: it discovers every apps/*/src, packages/*/src and apps/web/server.mjs file that starts a child (apps/desktop left out: the operator's own computer), checks node-pty and per-function option positions, refuses namespace imports, and names the two host git children as exact exceptions, so a new host spawn or a fixed one fails it; it fails on space-db-cleanup.mjs:151 before the fix and on browser-sandbox.ts:30 or node-pty-spawn.ts:12 with their env removed. Closed with evidence: node-pty-spawn.ts (the API always sends buildCliEnvironment's allowlist; apps/api/tests/child-process-env.test.ts plants the session secret, database URL, internal and connector tokens and OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini keys and finds none in any runtime's PTY env, NORMAL or LOGIN, and fails when one is injected; sudo's env_keep for the wrappers names no Space credential); the queue daemon (space-merge-queue.service loads no .env, only HOME and PATH); the public container, read only on the oll4com/spaceapp checkout feat/opencode2-installer 6023bc7 (deploy/docker unchanged against its origin/main): core-supervisor passes the secrets only to the api, worker and web services, and apps/web/server.mjs reads only SPACE_WEB_HOST and spawns nothing. The safe-child-process guard was red on dev (browser-sandbox.ts imports child_process; its spawn passes childProcessEnv()): it now leaves that Browser Host file to the AST guard, no host code changed. Remaining, exactly: (1) packages/cli-host/src/server.ts and packages/browser-host/src/server.ts run git rev-parse HEAD with the inherited env when SPACE_CLI_HOST_BUILD_COMMIT / SPACE_BROWSER_HOST_BUILD_COMMIT is unset: the same space user that already reads /opt/spaceapp/.env, so no privilege is crossed; the fix ships only with the guarded host restarts. (2) Outside the repo: /etc/systemd/system/space-copilot-shared.service (hand-installed 2026-10-11) starts copilot-shared-server.sh as spaceapp-user with EnvironmentFile=/opt/spaceapp/.env, which would put the session secret in an environ every agent can read; it is socket-activated on 127.0.0.1:43031 in netns space-cli-copilot, has accepted no connection, and no repository code uses it; removing the unit and socket (or that EnvironmentFile line) is a root change for the operator. The run-with-space-env exception stays as approved (its release runner's children use explicit allowlists in space-release-engine.mjs). 2026-11-02 later (goal e803a663, after 9a05944db3): the pane host git read (packages/cli-host/src/server.ts readCliHostBuildCommit) now passes only PATH and HOME, as the API git children do, and left the guard exception list; restoring the inherited env fails apps/worker/tests/child-process-env.test.ts (cli-host/src/server.ts:272 missing or raw env). The Browser Host read gets the same one-line fix on branch fix/browser-host-git-env (10c4c00de8, guard exception list then empty), which ships only with the guarded Browser Host restart: the dev queue refuses packages/browser-host/ at integration. Remaining: that Browser Host restart and the out-of-repo space-copilot-shared.service (the operator root change). 2026-11-02 later (goal e803a663): the Browser Host part is live on stable d962ff9a28 (fix/browser-host-git-env merged onto stable): guarded Browser Host restart at 23:09 UTC on 1/11, live:verify ok; on stable the worker guard's host exception list is empty. findings.observationSource: Internal review of public v1.1.5 (8a3e1f0), 2026-10-16
findings.affected: apps/api/src/browser-sessions.ts and browser-evidence.ts (--no-sandbox); public Dockerfile stage browser and packages/run-spaceapp/templates/compose.yml service spaceapp-browser (database-url secret, spaceapp-data volume)
findings.evidence: 2026-11-01 probe on public-host (Docker 26.1.5, AppArmor on) with the spaceapp-browser 1.2.0-nous.c1 image: Chromium's sandbox fails under Docker's default seccomp and under docker-default AppArmor; with Docker's default seccomp plus unshare/setns/clone and apparmor=unconfined (no-new-privileges kept) it runs sandboxed (renderers in their own user and PID namespaces). Log: ~/agent-workspace/active/20261102-int5-c-f3/sandbox-probe.txt
findings.disposition: Needs the browser image to run Chromium's sandbox (user namespaces or a separate browser container without the data volume). Browser-host change; not in 1.1.6. 2026-11-01 (plan clipboard:zJF0KEWRcCje, Nous: design only, no host or browser restart): ~/agent-workspace/active/20261102-int5-c-f3/design.md compares (A) Chromium's user-namespace sandbox in the image (a seccomp profile shipped with run-spaceapp, a start-up sandbox self-check that keeps --no-sandbox and says so in health when it fails, the same flag change on public-host's Browser Host) with (B) a separate Chromium container without the data volume or the database secret (a launcher, a private CDP network, shared upload and capture paths). Pick: A first. Its one real cost is the AppArmor relaxation (docker-default blocks the sandbox; a custom profile needs host root), which is a decision for the operator or Nous before the three-OS lab; B only if credential separation beyond it is required. 2026-11-01 decision (Nous): Option A with this ladder for public installs: (1) a custom AppArmor profile loaded by run-spaceapp when host root is available; (2) otherwise apparmor=unconfined only with an explicit opt-in, off by default; (3) otherwise today's --no-sandbox, named in health and run-spaceapp doctor. No setting relaxes AppArmor silently; Option B stays parked. Step 1 (public-host, this change): apps/api/src/browser-sandbox.ts starts one headless Chrome without --no-sandbox when the Browser Host starts (and before the API's first evidence capture); browser-sessions.ts and browser-evidence.ts drop --no-sandbox only when it exits cleanly with the page, and the Browser Host's health status carries sandbox {state, reason, checkedAt}. Guard: apps/api/tests/browser-sandbox.test.ts. It reaches stable's Browser Host only with the next guarded Browser Host restart (public-host passed the probe on 2026-11-01). Step 2, the public containers: INT5-C-F3-S2. 2026-11-01 later (Nous): keep Docker's default AppArmor profile; never ship apparmor=unconfined by default; the fallback to --no-sandbox logs one line. Step 1 is on dev (q-20261101-181305-6667); the log line follows. The limitation and how to enable the sandbox: INT5-C-F3-S2. 2026-11-03 check (plan clipboard:zJF0KEWRcCje step 4): step 1 is live on stable. It reached main with promote q-20261101-194210-2ecd (09f0e4f58e, 2026-11-01 19:42 UTC), the Browser Host (pid 625381) started after it on 2026-11-02 08:08 UTC, and none of its 72 pane Chrome processes runs with --no-sandbox, so no guarded Browser Host restart is needed. What remains is INT5-C-F3-S2 (the public containers, a release-train item).

findings.observation: A new pane's CLI starts automatically only while the browser's clock minus the server's pane createdAt is within 60 s, so a server clock that runs behind the browser leaves the Getting Started pane unstarted with no launch control on screen
findings.observationSource: 1.1.8 c1 vm219 scoped session, 2026-10-25: Docker Desktop's VM clock ran 1 h behind after the daylight-saving change; diagnosis in agent-workspace/active/20261025-1.1.8-devtest/vm219-scoped-root-cause.md
findings.reproduction: Create a pane on a server whose clock is more than 60 s behind the browser: GET /api/panes/<id>/cli/session answers null and the web never POSTs a start (pane_cli_sessions stays empty).
findings.evidence: 1.1.8 c1 lab evidence (windows-starter-workspace-1.1.8.json, windows-first-agent-diag.json); same code in 1.1.7
findings.disposition: Open (1.1.9, Nous decision 2026-10-25): measure the pane's age with the server's clock (the offset from API responses' Date header) instead of the browser's, with a test where the server runs 1 h behind. Pre-existing since 1.1.7; Docker Desktop VM clock drift (daylight-saving change, sleep) is the known trigger. Not in 1.1.9: the fix is planned for 1.1.10 (Nous decision 2026-10-26). Fixed 2026-10-27 (6115a41fa2 and b4b19939b7, plan clipboard:zJF0KEWRcCje step 7, Nous Warm approval): request() in apps/web/src/live-api.ts learns the server-clock offset (apps/web/src/server-clock.ts, outside the live API for the demo bundle) from each API response's Date header, skipping cached answers (Age header or 304), and TerminalPane's new-pane check uses serverNow() - createdAt; with no Date header seen it is the browser clock as before. Test: apps/web/tests/terminal-pane-server-clock.test.tsx (server 1 h behind: a just-created pane starts, a pane created 2 h ago does not, an Age header leaves the offset unchanged). Also fixed 2026-11-02 (9f05142c54, plan clipboard:NtzEOzE3Ew00): the pane working-time badge's cap at the pane's age (apps/web/src/features/pane-working-time/usePaneWorkingTime.ts) uses serverNow() - createdAt too, so a browser clock behind the server no longer reads a young pane's working time as 0m. Test: the UX-004 case in apps/web/tests/pane-working-time.test.tsx (browser 1 h behind: 20m stays 20m).

findings.observation: The public export rewrites the Monitoring Copilot's collector network (192.0.2.x, the maintainers' private bridge) to the documentation range 192.0.2.x, in the collector URL check and its defaults
findings.observationSource: Public export audit and review while cutting run-spaceapp 1.1.9 c3 (2026-10-27)
findings.reproduction: Export the source with the private rules and read monitoringCollectorUrlSchema in the exported contracts: it accepts only http://192.0.2.<host>:<port>.
findings.evidence: export audit of b628e7aa93 (2026-10-27); the MON-001 cases of packages/contracts/tests/monitoring-copilot.test.ts (the contract source names no 192.0.2. address) and apps/api/tests/monitoring-copilot.test.ts (an installation with no collector configured) fail on the old code; apps/web/tests/monitoring-copilot-pane.test.tsx
findings.disposition: Open (1.1.10): in public installs the Monitoring Copilot (an optional module, off by default) accepts only collectors in 192.0.2.x, so it cannot reach a real collector. Fix: take the collector network and default URLs from configuration that the maintainers' instance sets, empty in public builds, instead of code. 1.1.9's tests use neutral addresses so the exported suite still checks the same rules. 2026-11-03, 495a490956 (deployed to dev by ticket q-20261103-045116-0a16): the contract accepts any private IPv4 collector URL and keeps no network or defaults; the API reads SPACE_MONITORING_COLLECTOR_NETWORK and SPACE_MONITORING_COLLECTOR_HOST (stable's 192.0.2.0/24 and 192.0.2.210 in deploy/space-api.service, which the public export does not ship), narrows settings and the client to that network (409 outside it) and fills empty URLs from the host's defaults; unset, a public install sets its collector in Setup.

findings.observation: The public export rules rewrite the maintainers’ private domains only in their plain form; the same name written regex-escaped (a backslash before each dot) passes the rewrite and the export audit unchanged
findings.observationSource: Cutting run-spaceapp 1.1.9 c6 (2026-10-28): an exported API test kept a private mail address inside a regular expression while its plain strings were rewritten to example.invalid, so the public suite failed that case
findings.affected: scripts/public-export-private-rules.json (private rules) and the export audit; apps/web/src/features/sensitive-data/SensitiveDataMask.tsx (the internal-domain pattern names a maintainer domain, public since before 1.1.9)
findings.reproduction: Export a source file whose regular expression holds a private domain with escaped dots: the plain-form rule does not match it and the audit for remaining private names does not flag it.
findings.evidence: c6 cut of 4f01583e71 (2026-10-28): scoped vitest failure in apps/api/tests/nous.test.ts; fixed in the source by d077b0ff0c (a neutral address), which 1.1.9 c7 carries; 2026-11-01: scripts/tests/public-export-private-rules.test.mjs (fails on the old rules); the public exporter run on dev with the old rules exported 6 files holding an escaped private runtime path (\/opt\/spaceapp in regular expressions: apps/api/src/decisions-service.ts, packages/cli-host/src/session-registry.ts, packages/runtime/src/store.ts and three tests) unchanged, with the new rules it rewrites them; report ~/agent-workspace/reports/20261102-exp-001; apps/web/tests/sensitive-data-mask.test.tsx (EXP-001 case)
findings.disposition: Open (after 1.1.9): make each private-name rule and the audit also match the regex-escaped form (a backslash before each dot), and move the SensitiveDataMask internal-domain list to configuration so the public build carries none. 1.1.9 is not affected beyond the SensitiveDataMask pattern that was already public. 2026-11-01 (plan clipboard:zJF0KEWRcCje, goal e803a663): escaped forms done in scripts/public-export-private-rules.json, the data the public exporter reads. Every rewrite and audit pattern accepts any number of backslashes before a dot (a regex literal's one, a RegExp string's two); the audit rules also accept them before a slash. The path, URL and IP rewrites capture those backslashes and put them back (`$1/opt$2/spaceapp`), so a rewritten regex literal still parses and an escaped IP keeps its escaped dots. Exporting dev with the old rules left 6 files with escaped `\/opt\/spaceapp` paths in the public tree (shipped in 1.1.9); the new rules rewrite them and the export passes its audit. No exporter change; it takes effect at the next export. Still open: the SensitiveDataMask internal-domain list (a maintainer domain, public since before 1.1.9) moving to configuration. 2026-11-03 (goal e803a663, plan clipboard:zJF0KEWRcCje step 4): the SensitiveDataMask list names no maintainer domain any more. Instead of a configured list, the mask hides the registrable domain the page is served from (instanceDomain: tldts with private suffixes, null for localhost and IPs), plus its subdomains, bare or in URLs. The maintainers' instance still masks its own domain, a public install masks its own, and the source carries none. tldts was already in the web entry chunk, so the bundle does not grow. Test: the EXP-001 case of apps/web/tests/sensitive-data-mask.test.tsx (own-domain forms, a look-alike left alone, no domain without a host, no maintainer domain in the source); it failed before the change. Takes effect in the public tree at the next export.

findings.disposition: Recorded only (Nous 3/11: a ticket only when it is next due by registry order; P0/P1 items come first). Fix: the smoke tells a plan or entitlement answer (403) from missing or expired credentials and Space shows the plan state ('the Kimi subscription has no Kimi Code'), with no login prompt. 2026-11-03 (goal e803a663, plan clipboard:zJF0KEWRcCje step 4): the provider's answer, read again from the smoke on stable (kimi 2.4.1): "provider.auth_error: 403 Your current subscription does not have access to Kimi Code right now. Upgrade your plan ...". deploy/kimi-vscode-parity's smoke reads it as NO_PLAN (prints SPACE_KIMI_NO_PLAN), writes the verified-version marker with that state, and credential-status answers NO_PLAN; a login with stored credentials on such a plan runs the smoke and stops there, so no login prompt opens. The API (cli-runtimes.ts parseCredentialStatus) shows the runtime UNAVAILABLE with no login button and the reason "Kimi Code CLI is signed in, but the Kimi Code Subscription plan has no access to it. Upgrade the plan with the provider, then check it again in Setup; signing in again will not help." After an upgrade, Setup's check reruns the smoke and rewrites the marker READY. Setup's own check still reports that run as "Provider failed" (no plan-specific outcome there). Tests, each failing without the fix: the ADAPTER-011 case of apps/api/tests/cli-runtimes-host.test.ts (the real 403 text through run_login and credential_status) and the NO_PLAN lines of the Kimi registry case in apps/api/tests/cli-runtimes.test.ts.

findings.observation: Stable and dev share ~/.hermes, so a Hermes shared gateway that a pane of one instance started is discovered by the other's Hermes TUIs even in a network namespace they cannot reach: stable's Hermes panes (VPN broker namespace) retried every 30 s with 'reconnecting…' and every prompt queued while a gateway a dev pane started ran in the host namespace
findings.observationSource: P8 runtime live proofs on stable a54d717a87 and dev 6323fdcd8c, 2026-11-04 (plan clipboard:NtzEOzE3Ew00 step 9)
findings.affected: deploy/hermes-vscode-parity (one HERMES_HOME, ~/.hermes, for both instances; the gateway discovery is Hermes 0.22's own), the dev pane host (host network namespace) and stable's space-cli-vpn-broker (its own namespace)
findings.reproduction: Open a Hermes pane on dev (it starts `hermes gateway run --idle-exit` in the host network namespace and registers it in ~/.hermes), then a Hermes pane on stable while that gateway runs: the stable TUI logs 'attached shared gateway discover url=ws://127.0.0.1:<port>' and 'transport exit code=1006' every 30 s, shows 'reconnecting…' and queues the prompt. Ending the dev-started gateway lets the stable TUIs start their own and recover.
findings.evidence: ~/agent-workspace/reports/20261104-plan-NtzEOzE3Ew00-step9-p8/summary.json; ~/agent-workspace/reports/20261104-plan-NtzEOzE3Ew00-step9-p8/hermes-gateway/ (netns.txt: gateway net:[4026531840], stable TUIs net:[4026533174]; tui-attach-excerpt.txt; gateway_state-before.json, code_version 0.22.6); ~/.hermes/logs/tui_gateway_crash.log 2026-11-04 05:52-05:57 UTC; ~/agent-workspace/reports/20261104-adapter-012/ (profile-before.txt, profile-after.txt, hermes-before.txt, hermes-after.txt); ~/agent-workspace/reports/20261104-adapter-012-013-stable/summary.json (hermes-state-0..5*.txt, s1-*, s2-started.txt, d1-*, d2-*)
findings.disposition: Recorded (P8). Mitigated by hand once: SIGTERM to the leftover dev-started gateway (pid 3274303) at 05:56 UTC; stable's TUIs recovered at 05:57:10 on a gateway in their own namespace. No operator Hermes pane was in the log in that window. Fix direction: give dev its own Hermes home or gateway state so the instances never discover each other's gateway, or have the wrapper refuse a discovered gateway it cannot reach. Until then a Hermes test on dev can block stable's Hermes panes until that gateway idles out. 2026-11-04 fix (branch fix/adapter-012-hermes-dev-home, plan clipboard:NtzEOzE3Ew00 step 9): dev panes run the Hermes profile space-dev with gateway.standalone: true, so its gateway is its own and the root's never serves it. The profile resolves tools and installs to the root's (no rebuild), links .env, auth.json, SOUL.md and skills, and copies config.yaml when stable's changes; sessions, memories, cron and the gateway are dev's. The API sets SPACE_CLI_INSTANCE=dev only for dev's CLIs, kept by deploy/zz-space-cli-env.sudoers; stable is unchanged. deploy/hermes-vscode-parity hermes_instance_home refuses to start a dev pane whose profile is not standalone. Dev panes run /opt/spaceapp/bin (SPACE_CLI_COMMAND_PATH), so the change reaches them when stable's deploy installs the wrapper and sudoers (promote). Component proof on public-host (Hermes 0.22.6): a TUI on that profile started a gateway whose state says 'this profile is standalone (gateway.standalone: true); it serves only itself'; the root's gateway files, facts.json and dependency environments were unchanged. During the first experiment, a test home that linked installs without tools committed a dependency generation built on that home's Python; no Hermes process ran, and `hermes pm repair` plus `hermes pm install` on the root committed a5ff8de… on ~/.hermes/tools again (the stray generation is unselected and Hermes collects it after 24 h). Tests: scripts/tests/hermes-dev-profile.test.mjs (4, fail before), the SPACE_CLI_INSTANCE case in apps/api/tests/child-process-env.test.ts. Stays partial until the live proof after promote: a dev Hermes pane, then a stable Hermes pane that reaches ready. 2026-11-04 live proof on stable f43062d9cf (promote q-20261104-082230-f66e) and dev: a stable Hermes pane started the root gateway in the VPN namespace; a dev Hermes pane then created ~/.hermes/profiles/space-dev (gateway.standalone: true) and ran its own gateway (HERMES_HOME=profile, SPACE_CLI_INSTANCE=dev) in the host namespace with its own socket, lock and state.db; the root's gateway.lock and state.db stayed stable's. A new stable Hermes pane started while dev's gateway ran reached ready ('2 sessions') with no 'reconnecting…', and the first stayed ready. The live run found that the profile prefixes Hermes's prompt ('space-dev ❯') and Space Control refused every prompt to dev Hermes panes; fixed in apps/api/src/room-terminal-screen.ts (test in cli-composer-readiness.test.ts), ticket q-20261104-083317-7566, dev eca22499fa; prompts land since. Fixed.

findings.observation: Space Control's resume of a Hermes or OMP pane with no recorded native reference falls back to the TUI's /resume menu instead of the declared `--continue` fallback; on Hermes 0.22.5 and OMP 18.16.0 the task's title is not found there, the action fails and the pane is left in a fresh session with /resume typed
findings.observationSource: P8 runtime live proofs on stable a54d717a87 and dev 6323fdcd8c, 2026-11-04 (plan clipboard:NtzEOzE3Ew00 step 9)
findings.affected: apps/api/src/room-pane-cli-controller.ts resumeCli (the menu after 'Exact native resume is unavailable'), apps/api/src/room-cli-menu.ts; the descriptors declare `--continue` without a reference (apps/api/src/cli-runtime-descriptors.ts cli:hermes, cli:omp)
findings.reproduction: On dev, whose API records no Hermes or OMP native reference (as for Claude, its private PID namespace keeps the native reader from the pane's process), give a Hermes or OMP pane a word, quit it, then space_execute resume: FAILED 'The requested menu selection could not be verified; inspect the pane's current menu.', a new Space session starts and the old conversation is not reopened.
findings.evidence: ~/agent-workspace/reports/20261104-plan-NtzEOzE3Ew00-step9-p8/summary.json (hermes-a-resume.json, hermes-a-after-resume.txt, omp-a-resume.json, omp-a-resumed.txt); ~/agent-workspace/reports/20261104-adapter-013-live/ (c3-*); ~/agent-workspace/reports/20261104-adapter-012-013-stable/summary.json (s1-resume*, d1-resumed.txt, d2-*, o-*)
findings.disposition: Recorded (P8). On stable, where the reference is recorded, the same resume is exact (Hermes LP pass 2026-11-04). Fix direction: without a recorded reference resume through the launcher's declared `--continue`, and keep the menu for runtimes that have none. 2026-11-04 fix (branch fix/adapter-013-resume-no-menu, plan clipboard:NtzEOzE3Ew00 step 9): apps/api/src/room-pane-cli-controller.ts resumeCli no longer opens /resume for Hermes or OMP. Without a recorded reference they continue in a fresh session with the task's bounded context (SPACE_FALLBACK, the path task history already uses; another pane's newest session is never picked). With a reference they still resume exactly; with no task named a fresh session starts. Claude keeps its title picker. Test: the ADAPTER-013 case in apps/api/tests/room-pane-cli-controller.test.ts (fails before the change). Live proof on dev follows the deploy. 2026-11-04 live proofs: stable f43062d9cf, Hermes with its recorded reference: Space resume NATIVE_RESUME reopened the original conversation, no menu. Dev 60382d74fb, Hermes and OMP without a reference: SPACE_FALLBACK into a fresh session, the context submitted to the model (the gateway answered 429), composer clear, no menu. The runs found four more defects on this path, fixed on dev with a test each: the prompt read only from the newest 200 transcript chunks, so a retry spinner made the task 'not resumable' (unified-cli-task-registry.ts, q-20261104-073406-08ae); omp's large-paste menu held the context (pane-cli-resume.ts, q-20261104-075339-f12e); SGR and mode parameters left in the context (codex-history-titles.ts, q-20261104-080805-e8a7); Hermes kept the context as an unsent draft (submitCliPrompt, tests/cli-shared-context-submit.test.ts, q-20261104-084632-de34, dev 60382d74fb; reaches stable at the next promote). One OMP resume answered UNKNOWN 'CLI readiness has not been confirmed' while its pane ran the turn; the next run answered COMPLETED. OMP on stable stays off (operator). Fixed.
